Repository: re-cinq/HALEngine
Ticket: #93 Report usage across every tool round, not just the last

The pull request for this ticket has a RED build. Your job is to make it
green, on the branch you are already on, and nothing else.

The ticket's branch is checked out with write access at /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/target.
Run every command from inside it (`cd /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/target` first). The ticket
is at `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/ticket.md`: read it before anything else. Pass `repo` (the
owner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has
no checkout to detect it from.

CI is the judge of this branch, and the `CI reported failures` section
of `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/round-brief.md` is its verdict: the sha it judged, the checks that failed, and for
each — when CI published them — the annotations (`path:line message`),
the step that failed, and what it printed. Start from it, not from a
full local build.

WHEN THE VERDICT NAMES A FILE AND LINE — an annotation such as
`specs/x/spec.md:7 Status "draft" does not match ...` — open that file
at that line and fix what it says. Do not install dependencies, build
the workspace, or run the suite to confirm a finding CI already made
about a specific line; a lint or status error on a markdown file needs
an editor, not `npm ci`. Run a command only when the FIX needs one: a
test you must see fail, a typecheck of a package whose code you changed.
When that command's toolchain is not in this pod (`java`, `mvn`,
`gradle`, `go`, `cargo` or `dotnet` is not found), do not look for it and
do not install it: fix from the verdict, push, and let CI judge the push.

When it names the failed STEP and what that step printed but no
annotation, that is the diagnosis: find that step in
`.github/workflows/` and run only that step's command. When it names
only a check, map the check name to the job that publishes it, find the
command that job runs, and run ONLY that. Reproducing the whole build to
rediscover what you have already been told costs the ticket a pod and
tells you nothing new. The pod's Bash hook refuses a test runner given
no path, no workspace flag and no `cd` into the step's directory, so a
repo-wide `vitest run` never starts.

RUN A STEP'S COMMAND WHERE CI RAN IT, never from wherever your shell
happens to be. When the report says `Ran as: npm script <script> of
package <package>` (`npm_script` in `lore_get_ci_failures`), run
`npm run <script> -w <package>` from the repository root — or plain
`npm run <script>` if <package> is the root package.json's own name.
For any other step, take the directory from the workflow step itself
(its `working-directory:`, a `cd`, or a `-w`/`--prefix` in its `run:`).
A package's test command run at the repo root is NOT that command:
`npx vitest run` there discovers every package's suite. Run 754cb4fa ran
nine suites with coverage for 43 minutes and hit its deadline answering
what one package's suite answers in minutes.

NEVER RUN THE LINTER IN THIS POD, scoped or not. CI ran it on a machine
sized for it; here a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against a 1Gi
pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on it. When the red
check is a lint or format job, its findings are what you fix, not what
you reproduce: take the file and line from the annotation, or ask CI
with `lore_get_ci_failures` and then `lore_get_ci_job_log` with
`grep: "error"`. Format only the files this branch changed
(`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`); typecheck nothing here —
CI's build step already did, and it does not fit this pod.

IF THE SECTION IS MISSING OR TOO THIN, ASK CI YOURSELF: call
`lore_get_ci_failures` with `repo` (owner/name) and `branch` (the output
of `git branch --show-current`) — it reports on that branch: the judged
sha, the conclusion, and each failed check with its annotations, failed
steps and log tail. When a failure needs more of its log, call
`lore_get_ci_job_log` with `repo` and that failure's `job_id`, a `grep`
for the report's error marker (`error`, `FAIL`, `✖`) and a small `tail`.
Never reinstall or rebuild the workspace to learn what CI already
printed.

FIRST, check the branch has not moved since CI judged it. The section's
heading names the sha CI read (`judged_sha` from `lore_get_ci_failures`
when the section is absent); run `git log --format=%s <that sha>..HEAD`.
If any commit it lists does not carry `[skip ci]`,
the branch moved after CI judged it: somebody pushed, and CI has not
judged the new head yet.
Change nothing and run nothing, and end with
LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"branch moved past <sha>; CI re-judges the head"}}
The wait re-reads CI on the new head and sends the branch back here only
if that is red too.

BEFORE YOU READ ANY FILE, ask the graph what has failed here before.
For every path the red output names, call `lore-query-trace` with
`failures_touching` set to that path. Each row is a previous failed
attempt on that file: what failed, on which commit, and — when a later
attempt fixed it — the sha that did. `git show` that sha. This repo has
very likely hit this exact error before, and the diff that ended it last
time is the cheapest thing you will read today.

A row that says `still open` was never fixed; treat it as a warning that
the obvious fix did not work before, not as a solution to copy.

RULES:
- Fix EVERY finding the verdict names, in this visit, in the order
  listed. There is no local re-run here that would reveal the rest, and
  each finding you leave costs the ticket a round: run 2a291314's repair
  fixed one of three and the build came back red twice more. Do not add
  speculative fixes for failures the verdict did not name.
- Fix the cause, not the symptom. Never delete, skip, `.only`, `.todo` or
  loosen a test to go green; never widen a type to `any` to silence a
  typecheck error; never add an eslint-disable to pass lint. If the test
  is genuinely wrong, say why in your final message before you change it.
- Change only what the red build requires. Unrelated edits make the
  re-review harder and are not what was asked.
- If the named check's command passes locally, say exactly what you ran
  and what passed — the failure may be environment-only, and that is a
  finding, not a fix.

DELIVERY, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the next step runs in a DIFFERENT container:
- Before you commit, run the repository's FORMATTER over the files you
  changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`, `gofmt -w <files>`, whichever
  this repo uses) and nothing else from CI's checklist. Do NOT run the
  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not
  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against
  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly
  that. A lint finding comes back as a red build naming the file and
  line, which the next round fixes with an editor.
- Do NOT typecheck here either. A green test is not a compiled build —
  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build
  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on
  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's
  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build
  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next
  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.
- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a
  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from
  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and
  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it
  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.
- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a
  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/429c46d0f998/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries
  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token
  and must never look for one.
- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`
  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.
  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no
  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build
  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`
  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.
- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of
  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and
  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.
- If you changed nothing because the branch moved, end as the FIRST check
  above says. If you changed nothing for any other reason, say why and
  report `changes_requested` below, never `failed`: a failed repair ends
  the ticket, and the branch may already be green.
- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore
  opens the PR from the branch you push.

Print exactly one of these as the last line of your final message:
- You reproduced a failure, fixed it, and the build passes locally:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"<one line: what was broken>"}}
- You could not make it green, or the failure is not in this repository:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"changes_requested","extras":{"ci_blocked":"<one line: what you ran and what stayed red>"}}

<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/hal-engine-tool-budget/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.52" tokens="172">
# Tool Budget

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#56, re-cinq/HALEngine#57, re-cinq/HALEngine#50 |
| Status | Implemented          |

The tool loop used to run `round <= maxToolRounds`, which is six iterations at the default of five, and the sixth executed tools whose results no provider call would ever read: the results were pushed onto `messages`, the loop ended, and the generator returned. Real data was fetched and paid for, and the model never saw it. `maxToolRounds` is now a gate immediately before tool execution rather than the loop's own condition, so every executed round is read by a following provider call.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Agent Memory" source="memories" priority="2">
<document source="session-summary/2026-09-09-ci-judged-implementation-loop" type="memory" tokens="870">
**session-summary/2026-09-09-ci-judged-implementation-loop** (memory): Goal: cut GKE cost by moving test/lint execution off implementation-loop agent pods onto GitHub Actions. Shipped as PRs #1905, #1909, #1911.

DESIGN. New `await-ci` park node (type `ci_check`) after `tdd-round`. Rounds leave through it on success and changes_requested alike; `tdd-round` loses its self-edge and the 12-round budget moves to `await-ci -> tdd-round` (iteration_max keys on `${from}->${to}`). A park dispatches no Agent CR, so waiting costs nothing.

WHY A NEW STATION TYPE, NOT A SECOND pr_review NODE. Four call sites key on the node TYPE. The decisive one is decideMarkReady (spec-pr.ts), which flips a PR out of draft when the DESTINATION node type is pr_review — a pr_review round-wait would un-draft after round one and start code review on unfinished work. Also keyed on type: loop-run-closed.ts, backlog-ticket.ts, the stations registry test, the web-ui HUMAN_STATIONS mirror.

THE [skip ci] TRAP (load-bearing). This repo's pr-checks format job auto-commits `style: prettier [skip ci]` to the PR branch. Once pods stop formatting, that commit lands on nearly every push, GitHub creates no checks for it, and ciConclusion(head) returns "none" forever. So verdicts read ciJudgedSha = newest commit carrying no skip-CI marker, not the head. Applied to the end-of-line await-pr wait too.

FEEDBACK CHANNEL. pr-ready-check reports {ci_feedback_sha, ci_failed_checks, ci_failure_summary} in resume args; resume-event-handler merges args BEFORE the walk advances; withCiFeedback appends a prompt block. It renders only when the incoming visit is changes_requested, because args persist after being acted on.

WIRING GOTCHA. The prompt is resolved in resolveNodeDispatch, called from advance-line.ts dispatchForNode — NOT in nodeLaunchSpec. Passing ciFeedback to the latter was silently dead. Unit tests stayed green; the implementation-loop acceptance harness caught it, which is exactly the composition layer it exists for.

PROMPTS. Format-step instruction removed from all seven delivering recipes. tdd-round runs only the acceptance tests plus the one test it writes. pr-ready re-runs nothing. fix-ci is handed failed check NAMES instead of reproducing install/lint/typecheck/build/test. Production runs lore.agent_definitions rows, so migration 0067 rewrites the seven org prompts conditionally and emits a catalog event each; catalog-seed.yaml regenerated.

TRADE-OFF. Pod minutes fall; GitHub Actions minutes rise (one PR-checks run per round, ~20 jobs); wall-clock per ticket grows by one CI run plus up to the 2-minute sweep interval. No pre-merge baseline of station_runs durations was captured.

REVIEW. Five bot findings across the stack. Four declined with reasons: masking lore/ checks inside the shared ciConclusion would break auto-merge and the end-of-line review-in-flight guard (the masking belongs only in the per-round verdict); octokit types check_run.output as required, so a null guard is dead code the no-unnecessary-condition rule rejects. One acted on: the truncation cap in withCiFeedback was kept and pinned by a test, since it guards the boundary where resume-event args become a prompt.

PROCESS. Inserting one test shifted spec anchors repo-wide; re-anchor by mapping the enclosing test TITLE through a git base ref, never by offset, and never twice over the same links. `npx eslint .` OOMs and exits 0 — use NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 with --quiet.
</document>
<document source="session:re-cinq/lore#2039" type="episode" tokens="47">
**session:re-cinq/lore#2039** (episode) [observed]: PR #2039 adds MCP tools lore_get_ci_failures and lore_get_ci_job_log to inspect CI failures and logs, keyed on branch name or PR number.
</document>
<document source="session-summary/2026-09-12-repair-build-ci-verdict" type="memory" tokens="663">
**session-summary/2026-09-12-repair-build-ci-verdict** (memory): Diagnosed assembly run 997026f5 (implementation-loop, issue #1510, PR #1684) and shipped PR #2039.

FINDING: the run did not die running tests. Four rounds came back red on ONE job (format) for ONE eslint error (specs/testing-standards/spec.md:7 require-status-matches-coverage). await-ci returned `failed` (ci_red_unchanged) → repair-build. ciFeedbackOf (apps/floor/src/work/assembly-run/ci-feedback.ts) rendered the "CI reported failures" block only for incoming outcome changes_requested; the await-ci→repair-build edge fires on failed. So repair-build — the node the YAML says "is handed the failing checks" — got NO verdict, ran `npm ci` + `npm run build -w @re-cinq/lore-shared`, and died at the 1Gi pod limit (BackoffLimitExceeded) on a one-line fix. ci_failure_summary was "" because Actions check-run output is null; #2021 (09-11, after the run) added steps+tail; the annotations endpoint had the exact path:line message and nothing read it.

SHIPPED (#2039, 4 commits): gate widened to failed+changes_requested; JobFailure.annotations (failure level, paginated) rendered first; explainFailedChecks moved from stations park-readers to shared check-runs.ts; new port reads listBranchCommits(repo, branch, limit) oldest-first + jobLog; lore-api GET /api/repos/:o/:r/ci-failures?branch|pr_number and /ci-jobs/:job_id/log?tail&grep; MCP tools lore_get_ci_failures / lore_get_ci_job_log in ci-tools.ts registered in registerSharedTools (agent gateway serves them), lore_get_pr_status moved beside them; detectCurrentBranch() in server-core repo-detect (uncached, null on detached HEAD). fix-ci prompt: act on annotation with an editor, ask CI via the tools, never reinstall/rebuild. NO migration: fix-ci org row is NULL since 0068 and resolves from the yaml in the image. OpenAPI + web-ui types + catalog seed regenerated; specs for both routes and both tools; FR15, shared-utilities, platform-infrastructure amended.

DECISIONS: user first got my "keep reads Floor-side, no pod tools" recommendation, reaffirmed pod tools → treated as their call; then asked for branch-keyed inputs (a pod never reliably knows a PR number) → routes accept branch or pr_number, tool defaults branch from git.

TRAPS: max-lines (300) hit on platform-github.ts (two-port adapter) → file-level eslint-disable with justification. Link re-anchoring needed a HEAD-line+title script handling empty labels, backticked labels, repo-root paths, untracked spec files, duplicate titles; run prettier BEFORE relink. memory-tools/pipeline-tools mcp tests fail locally pre-existing (clean HOME too) — judge by CI.
</document>
<document source="session-summary/2026-09-09-run-page-workbench" type="memory" tokens="480">
**session-summary/2026-09-09-run-page-workbench** (memory): PR #1939 (feat/run-page-workbench) squash-merged 2026-09-09 as ad53a0ce4. Run detail page overhaul: (1) the run-viz SSE stream moved from the Floor to lore-api at GET /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream, multiplexing agent_event / node_status / run_status / task_event / ci_check / catchup_complete frames; fan-out is Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY via AFTER triggers (migration 0070, channel lore_run_stream, ids-only payloads) on a dedicated pg.Client outside the pool; only agent_event frames carry an SSE id so Last-Event-ID stays the agent_run_events row id and state types are re-sent as snapshots on reconnect. RunAutoRefresh polling and the Floor stream route/bus are deleted. ADR-037 amended. (2) Graph + persistent side panel with auto-selected node, model badge per station from the resolved agent catalog with definition fallback. (3) Claude Code terminal-style transcript with tool calls paired to results and task events folded in as system lines; Timeline card, replay scrubber and Event Timeline removed. (4) Definition of Done card: reads .lore/dod.md at branch HEAD only while the run is open, matches acceptance tests against the latest lore-code-trace report persisted in pipeline.test_reports (migration 0069, written by the Floor ci-tests hook), file-granular, labelled "as reported by CI". (5) Per-file PR diffs via GET /api/repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/files and PullRequestsPort.listFileChanges. Lessons: deleting a module that a vitest.config.ts coverage include names fails the declared-paths check; inserting one line in a test file shifts every later spec anchor in that file (shift with a perl one-liner on the specs); a `test(...)` fixture helper in a test file is read by require-spec-link as a test block; specs were amended in place (run-viz FR2/FR4.14-18/FR7/FR8, implementation-loop FR16, platform FR-19.6) instead of adding new spec files.

{"results":[{"key":"re-lint/adoption-in-single-package-repo-2026-09-09","value":"Adopted @re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint@1.3.0 in re-cinq/HAL-engine (PR #17), then reconciled it against re-cinq/lore and re-cinq/bowman-ui. Read this before adopting re-lint anywhere else.

ORG CONVENTION: WIRE RULES BY HAND, NEVER configs.recommended. Both lore and bowman-ui enumerate each rule explicitly. bowman-ui states the reason: "wired by hand rather than through its preset so an upstream addition never switches itself on" — with --max-warnings 0 a preset turns `npm update` into a red build nobody asked for. HAL first used the preset and was rewritten.

THE DEFECT A PRESET HID: re-lint/no-forwarding-class is type-aware and INERT without parserOptions.projectService (or projectService/tsconfigRootDir). It sat at `error` in HAL and could not fire on any input; every run passed. lore sets projectService:true; bowman-ui leaves it inert but DOCUMENTS that. Always pair it with type info or don't wire it.

CANARIES ARE THE ORG CONVENTION FOR THIS. lore: tools/eslint-canaries/pkg + scripts/check-eslint-canaries.sh, lints with --no-ignore and fails if a rule stops reporting. bowman-ui: tests/fixtures/eslint-* + 4 test suites. Without one, a quiet rule is indistinguishable from clean code — which is exactly how the inert rule above survived. HAL now mirrors lore's script. Canary gotcha: no-forwarding-class needs a CONSTRUCTOR-INJECTED port (`constructor(private readonly inner: Inner) {}`) with an empty ctor body and every method forwarding 1:1 — a field initializer does NOT trip it. Also give the canary package its own tsconfig.json so projectService finds type info there.

QUEUE SHAPES DIFFER BY REPO, PICK BY THE GATE: lore parks at `warn` with counts in comments (its lint script has NO --max-warnings 0, so warn is a resting state; all its queues are now drained). bowman-ui has no queue — it adopted only rules it already passed. A repo with --max-warnings 0 AND real debt (HAL: 422 findings) needs a third shape: leave queued rules unwired and add a ratchet script that applies them on demand and fails if a count rose or hit zero.

QUEUE MEASUREMENT TRAP (cost two wrong baselines): the preset scopes rules to test files (max-expects, no-nondeterministic-tests on; max-lines-per-function, max-statements, no-magic-numbers OFF for tests). Re-enabling through one unscoped block read 32 for max-lines-per-function vs the preset's 16. Passing an outer `files` through `extends` REPLACES each extended config's globs — moved max-comment-lines 15->16 and no-magic-numbers 12->0 (rule silently off while the config still named it). Copy the preset's own files+options per queued rule, off-blocks included.

no-cross-layer-import: folderIn() requires a `<pkg>/src/` prefix, so a single-package repo with sources at <root>/src cannot be described — every file resolves to "not governed" and the rule reports 0 while looking adopted. Workaround: root = path.dirname(import.meta.dirname), package key = path.basename(import.meta.dirname), both derived. lore uses a real layers.yaml because it is a monorepo (keys apps/floor, libs/shared); a single-package repo cannot, since the loader walks UP from the linted file. Also needs a '.' entry for the barrel/composition root or those files may import nothing (58 findings in HAL).

MARKDOWN RULES: SCOPE TO SPECS, NOT REPO-WIDE. bowman-ui scopes require-intro-paragraph to specs/**/spec.md + adrs/*.md and require-status-matches-coverage to specs/**/spec.md. Measured repo-wide, require-status-matches-coverage looks like a Lore-only convention (21 in HAL); scoped it is 10 — one per spec, each missing a status row. require-statement-links (831 in HAL) IS genuinely Lore-specific; decline it rather than queue it. Status format: any line whose pipe-split second cell is "status", e.g. `| Status | Draft |`; buckets Draft / In Progress / Shipped / Rejected / Retired. Status is DERIVED from ([validated by](test.ts#Lnn)) link coverage, not from whether code merged — zero links means Draft even for shipped work, so say so in the doc or it reads as "unstarted". require-spec-link is the same debt from the tests' side (57 in HAL).

jscpd: BOTH repos run it (.jscpd.json). lore threshold 5 + mode mild + pattern-scoped; bowman-ui threshold 0, path ["."], in CI. GOTCHA: jscpd resolves a config's relative `path`/`pattern` against the CONFIG FILE's directory — running `jscpd --config ../other-repo/.jscpd.json` measures THAT repo, not yours. A "0 clones" reading for HAL was actually bowman-ui (81 .tsx files; HAL has none). HAL really has 7 clones / 2.2%.

.lore/test-commands.yml is the lore_list_tests / lore_run_test interface, NOT a list of CI commands — use the lore-test-commands skill. Shape: list / run (with {selector}) / coverage_format / cwd / path_prefix_strip (lore, flat) or a list of suites with id/name/description (bowman-ui). For Jest: --listTests prints FILES not tests, so parse *.test.ts with the TypeScript compiler and walk describe/it for names + line ranges; selector `<file>::<full name>`; ANCHOR the name into --testNamePattern (Jest treats it as a substring regex) and pass --coverageThreshold '{}' or a committed floor fails every single-test run.

OTHER DRIFT WORTH CHECKING IN ANY REPO: both repos lint `.` and format `.` (HAL was src/ only, so its own config and scripts were unchecked); both are on eslint ^10.10 / @eslint/js ^10 / typescript-eslint ^8.69+.
